A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AutoSchemaKG/ATLAS research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–G are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original triple-extraction, information-preservation, schema-induction, multi-hop QA, FELM, and MMLU results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds MMLU results for ToG operating on the ATLAS graphs.

M1.justification: The triple-extraction stages, contextual conceptualization, prompts, and retrieval algorithms remain unchanged in Sections 2–3 and Appendices A–E. The new pipeline diagram summarizes existing procedures; applying ToG to MMLU does not introduce a new algorithm.

E1.justification: The construction corpora, typing datasets, multi-hop QA benchmarks, FELM, and MMLU coverage are retained. Logic newly appears in the main MMLU table, but its tasks and results already appeared in v1 Tables 11–12.

E2.justification: Tables 7 and 12 add ATLAS+ToG alongside ATLAS+HippoRAG2 in the MMLU comparison for Wiki, Common Crawl, and Pes2o. ToG already appeared elsewhere, but these comparison entries are new. Existing external baselines remain; the BM25-to-DBM25 label change has no documented methodological counterpart.

E3.justification: Documented sampling, model, preprocessing, and per-task metric settings remain unchanged. However, Table 7 adds Logic to its summary and changes averages without explaining aggregation. V1's None average, 72.41, matches its seven subject scores; v2 reports 72.10 although its eight scores average 71.40. A changed aggregation protocol cannot be distinguished from reporting errors.

E4.justification: The information-preservation comparisons, entity/event/concept ablations, supplementary retrieval analyses, and case studies in Figures 9–10 are unchanged. The additional MMLU benchmark comparisons introduce no separate ablation, robustness test, or case study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Table 3's retained lower and upper bounds describe context conditions, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 12 adds ATLAS+ToG MMLU overall scores of 68.29, 68.40, and 68.97 for Wiki, CC, and Pes2o, plus subject-level results. Existing per-subject baseline and HippoRAG2 scores remain unchanged, while Table 7 averages and rankings change. The introduction also changes schema alignment from 95% to 92% without changing Table 4.

T1.justification: Definition 1, the graph mappings, and the mathematical definitions and equations in the appendices are unchanged. Added discussion of discourse structure provides conceptual motivation, without new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The revised contribution list claims ATLAS comprises the largest automatically constructed KGs and Graph RAG datasets, emphasizes the RAG pipeline, and drops the real-time-update claim. Autonomous schema induction remains central. The introduction narrows the alignment claim to 92%, while the abstract still states 95%.

C2.justification: The introduction adds explanations connecting event representations to proposition decomposition and hierarchical discourse paths. Section 5.4 expands the interpretation of Pes2o's domain strengths and highlights retrieval-method dependence in Logic. The limitations section and existing case-study interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation appendices, extraction and conceptualization prompts, hyperparameters, hardware specifications, GPU-hour estimates, and code/data access links remain unchanged. The added MMLU results include no additional reproduction instructions.

R1.justification: Sections 1 and 6 add connections to proposition-based representations, Dense X Retrieval, discourse-relation research, and earlier ontology work including WordNet, Hearst, Agirre, Txt2onto, and LLMs4OL. These additions broaden contextual positioning while retaining the existing related-work discussion.

P1.justification: The introduction and related-work discussion receive targeted expansions, four named contributions become three bullets, and the MMLU discussion is revised. The overall section organization and most methodological, experimental, and appendix prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 replaces the illustrative graph with a four-stage pipeline overview; the original example remains in Figure 10. Table 7 gains a Logic column and ToG rows, and Table 12 gains ToG rows with revised labels and highlighting. Other displays are retained with limited reflow.

improvement.justification: The pipeline overview improves methodological clarity, and the added MMLU comparison helps reveal retrieval-method dependence. However, v2 introduces an unreconciled 92% versus 95% alignment claim and unexplained Table 7 averages that, unlike v1's, do not match the displayed subject means. Without an aggregation explanation, the reliability of the revised summary comparisons is unclear. These benefits and reporting problems prevent a confident judgment of the net quality change.
